text:
sara: FYI bringing up arkus17b-int4 canary — seeing intermittent OOMs on warmstart and a small quality dip in evals. Anyone else hit this pattern?

mike: details? batch size, max_new_tokens, prefetch window?

sara: canary config pasted below, reproduced locally on a small dedicated pod:
```json
{"model":"arkus17b-int4","batch_size":8,"max_new_tokens":512,"prefetch_window":64,"kv_cache_policy":"lru"}
```

dylan: logs show repeated `kv_cache_eviction` spikes and then `alloc failed: out of memory` around token 1200 of long requests — mem frag seems likely. Also saw a ~1.6 ROUGE-L drop vs fp16 baseline in the nightly eval set.

eval-bot: arkus17b-int4 canary eval summary: throughput ok, mean latency +12% at p95, quality regression -1.8 ROUGE-L (512 tokens) vs baseline fp16. More details: https://internal.eval/arkus17b/3399990000

mike: two quick knobs: 1) reduce default max_new_tokens to 256 for the canary to limit large allocations; 2) lower prefetch window to 32 and batch_size to 4 for the int4 path while we tune eviction.

sara: ok i'll try a small canary change. also let's enable `kv_trim_threshold` to proactively free stale prefixes — dylan do we have a thermometer for kv churn?

dylan: yes, I can add a short metric: `kv_evictions_per_min` + `kv_live_frag_ratio`. initial numbers: evictions spiking to 700/min during warmstart bursts, frag ratio ~0.42.

mike: another idea: enable slow-start (gradual batch ramp) to avoid many concurrent warmstart allocations. our runtime supports `slow_start: {initial_batches:1, ramp_seconds:60}`.

sara: experimenting with this patch now. new canary config:
```json
{"model":"arkus17b-int4","batch_size":4,"max_new_tokens":256,"prefetch_window":32,"kv_trim_threshold":0.6,"slow_start":{"initial_batches":1,"ramp_seconds":60}}
```

deploy-bot: started canary deploy (arkus17b-int4) -> canary-arkus-03 with config hash abc123

anya: running smoke tests, will kick off eval suite once we have ~1000 tokens generated across requests.

eval-bot: quick sync: first 200 eval prompts: ROUGE-L diff now -0.4 vs fp16 (much better). p95 latency down 6%. No OOMs in the first 500 requests.

dylan: monitoring kv metrics — evictions down to ~120/min, frag ratio 0.18, allocations smoother. slow-start seems to have reduced concurrency spikes.

mike: if this holds, propose we make two changes for the int4 rollout: set model-level defaults to `max_new_tokens=256` and `prefetch_window=32`, keep batch_size suggestion at 4 for canaries, and enable kv_trim_threshold by default for int4 quant paths. We'll keep slow_start optional but recommend it in docs.

sara: agreed. i'll open a tiny RFC and a follow-up runbook for ops: steps to revert, metrics to watch (`kv_evictions_per_min`, `kv_live_frag_ratio`, `oom_count`, `eval_rouge_delta`).

deploy-bot: canary stable for 2h, no OOMs seen, autoscale ok.

anya: rolling changes to canary-configs repo, will trigger canary->staging promotion tomorrow if 24h stable.

sara: thanks team — nice fast loop. leaving the thread open for any late regressions, otherwise i'll mark follow-up in the RFC.
